idiom_name: function withResource<T, R>(open: () => T, body: (r: T) => R, close: (r: T) => void): R
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types to the same helper idiom: a generic signature keeps the resource type and the body's result linked, makes the teardown function mandatory at the call site, and lets the wrapper return exactly what the body returned. What replaces the classic structure is that typed higher-order function - and, on modern targets, the using declaration; the helper stays the choice for protocols with more than disposal (transaction, retry, metrics) and for code compiled to targets without explicit resource management. Type the close callback as returning void and accept unknown errors so implementations can be total, and provide an async overload that awaits the body before teardown.
pitfalls: Typing the body as (resource: T) => R but returning a bare R loses the link between resource and result; let both type parameters be inferred from the call site rather than annotating R alone.
An async body needs an overload returning Promise<R> and an await inside try; a synchronous wrapper returning a promise closes the resource before the work completes.
Structural typing accepts any object with the right shape - prefer the standard Disposable and AsyncDisposable interfaces so the helper and a using declaration agree on what can be disposed.

variants.name: using / await using with the Disposable and AsyncDisposable types
variants.idiom_name: using x = disposable; and await using x = asyncDisposable
variants.implementation_notes: TypeScript 5.2 implements the explicit resource management syntax: using and await using, the standard Disposable and AsyncDisposable interfaces, and the global DisposableStack and AsyncDisposableStack types. The compiler checks that the initializer is disposable and that await using appears in an async context, and it downlevels the syntax for targets below ES2022 while the types come from lib esnext.disposable - so the bracket is type-checked rather than merely conventional, which is the addition over the callback helper. Keep the helper for compound protocols and for code where the runtime symbols are not available.
pitfalls: Without target es2022-or-below plus the esnext.disposable lib (or polyfilled symbols) the keyword type-checks but the emitted code fails at runtime on the missing well-known symbols.
Disposable describes disposal, not ownership: a typed reference can still be copied into an object that outlives the scope, leaving a disposed resource reachable.
Downlevel emit preserves semantics but not the shape: each declaration becomes its own try/finally, and mixing await using and using in one scope changes the order in which disposers run.
